name: Theme
author: brodgar
description: Example addon (033-ui-stylesheet C1a, extended by 035-ui-chrome C2 and 036-ui-layout E): A CLIENT THEME THAT IS DATA, NOT CODE — text, chrome AND layout. Everything this addon looks like lives in theme.json next to main.lua — main.lua never names a surface, a font, a size, a colour, a pixel or a place; it reads the file, maps the two values JSON cannot hold to handles, and hands the whole table to the sheet's own data door. To make a different theme you edit the JSON. Three ordinary doors, one line each: hafen.asset('theme.json') is the FILE this addon ships (a 'data' asset, 033.3 — read as UTF-8 through :text(), sandboxed like every asset: absolute paths and '..' are rejected, D-017); hafen.json():parse turns the text into a table (a JSON array is 1-indexed, so [190,210,190] arrives as the sheet's own positional colour shape and needs no conversion); hafen.ui():sheet():load(t):install() installs it. EXACTLY TWO values in a rule are things JSON cannot carry, and both for the same reason — they are HANDLES: a font's `face` (a bare name is one of the client's built-ins, anything with a dot is a file this addon ships) and a border's or background's `image` (always a file this addon ships, here frame.png and panel.png). Both go through hafen.asset, the same door theme.json came through; a colour array, a 9-slice's four insets, a pad in pixels, an anchor's corner and a position are already the sheet's own shapes and are copied verbatim, so the chrome half of the theme costs three lines of Lua and the layout half costs none. The chrome rules are the C2 half: 'window.frame' carries bg + a 9-slice border + pad, so every window wears a dark slate frame whose 40 px top inset IS the title band the caption sits in (the engine adds no hidden room for a caption — a theme that wants a title bar says so in its own top inset), and 'panel' carries a thinner border for the framed surfaces that are not windows (the portrait, party avatars, list/info boxes, petals, dropdowns), which cannot re-lay themselves out and therefore take no pad. The layout rules are the E half: three selectors that name windows carry an `anchor`, so the inventory sits 8 px in from the screen's bottom-right corner, the equipment window from its top-right, and the character sheet is centred — derived from the live screen size rather than a remembered point, and a LAYER over the client's own positions rather than a write into them (the client still persists where the USER last dragged a window, so uninstalling this addon leaves nothing displaced). SAVING A LAYOUT IS THIS ADDON'S BUSINESS, NOT THE ENGINE'S: ':theme save' reads where the themed windows are right now and pins them through hafen.store (account scope, shared by every character), ':theme forget' drops the pins and the file's own anchors take over again — the whole profile system is a dozen lines here, because a sheet is plain data and an addon already has a store. DORMANT until you ask for it: ':theme on' wears it, ':theme off' takes it off, ':theme dump' lists what it styles and where it puts it — a theme installed at login would restyle your whole client on every login, which is not an example addon's decision to make. The sheet is OWNED: :reload or disabling this addon drops it and the stock client comes back, geometry included, and with a second styling addon the last one applied wins (D-043). Assets are interned, so an edit to theme.json takes effect on ':reload'. SAFE-tier: cosmetic, client-side, declares no permissions, sends nothing to the server.
